It does NOT test whether any of these has two or more block systems, so the witness Pass 5833 asked for is still not found. The divisibility pattern is observed on n = 7..16 only

pass_5840_scan.explanation: the incidence matrix of a cyclic configuration is a CIRCULANT, so its GF(2) rank is governed by gcd(1 + x^a + x^b, x^n - 1) over GF(2). The kernel is nonzero iff that gcd is nontrivial, which needs x^n - 1 to factor compatibly -- and 3 and 7 are the small n where x^n - 1 splits over GF(2) into factors a trinomial can meet
pass_5840_scan.pattern: nonzero kernels occur at n = 7, 9, 12, 14, 15 and NEVER at n = 8, 10, 11, 13, 16 -- exactly when 3 divides n or 7 divides n
pass_5840_scan.question: when is the GF(2) kernel of an n_3 cyclic configuration nonzero?
pass_5840_scan.status: CLASSICAL -- this is cyclic code theory, and by this session's own heuristic a short-proof statement about a classical object should have been searched before being measured. Recording it as an explanation found, not a result claimed
